record.title: OpenAI releases AI-generated mathematical research claims with specialist-led review groups
record.summary: On October 26, 2026, OpenAI announced three AI-generated research claims spanning harmonic analysis, computational complexity and quantum field theory, and described external expert-led groups to examine them. OpenAI says it publicly released manuscripts and Lean formalizations for local smoothing and an ETH refutation; a separate physics claim remains without public AI-produced artifacts. The official formalization catalog maps local-smoothing declarations to a Lean source file whose proof bodies invoke existing development theorems, and maps the ETH exact-counting theorem to a separate source file with a completed proof body. The linked ComparatorChallenges files contain `sorry` placeholders, but the repository instructions identify them as challenge configurations, so those placeholders alone do not refute formal proof coverage. This activation did not pin the repository revision, run Lean, audit dependencies or axioms, establish complete manuscript-to-formal correspondence, or obtain independent mathematical review. The theorem results therefore remain source-attributed claims with correctness, novelty and community acceptance unresolved.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: OpenAI published an October 26 announcement describing three AI-generated research claims and external expert-led groups to examine and explain them.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI claims its system proved local smoothing in every spatial dimension and lists Kakeya and Stein restriction consequences. The public formalization catalog maps related theorem declarations to OAI/Analysis/Fourier/LocalSmoothing/Comparator.lean, whose theorem bodies invoke existing development results. This activation did not build Lean, audit the dependency closure, or establish correspondence between every manuscript claim and the formal statements.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI claims its system refuted ETH and says Lean proves a fixed-k exact-counting result. The public formalization catalog maps exact_count_and_sat to OAI/Algorithms/SubexponentialSAT/SqrtLogSpace/Final.lean, where the theorem has a proof body. This activation did not run Lean, audit all dependencies/axioms, or establish that the formal statement fully matches the manuscript claim.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI says it has a mathematically rigorous existence result for certain four-dimensional interacting gauge theories including QCD and a unified completion of the Standard Model, but the expert group chose to withhold the AI-produced artifacts while preparing its own account.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The mathematical correctness, novelty, priority and independent acceptance of the announced results are not established by the inspected manuscripts, release, formalization catalog and source files; this activation did not build Lean or conduct an independent mathematical review.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The current GitHub main view of the ETH comparator challenge file defines exact_count_and_sat and its proof body ends in `sorry` at line 938. The official formalization catalog maps the result to a separate proof source, Final.lean; the challenge stub alone does not establish absence of a completed proof. No build or dependency audit was done.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The current GitHub main view of the local-smoothing comparator challenge file contains `sorry` bodies for six theorem entrypoints. The official catalog maps the related declarations to a separate source file whose proof bodies invoke existing development theorems; the challenge stub alone does not establish absence of a completed proof. No build or dependency audit was done.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: OpenAI’s ComparatorChallenges README describes challenge configurations as inputs to the comparator tool. Its formalization catalog separately maps the ETH theorem to SqrtLogSpace/Final.lean and local-smoothing declarations to LocalSmoothing/Comparator.lean. The inspected mapped files contain Lean proof terms for those declarations. The repository revision was not pinned and no build, dependency audit or axiom check was run.

contradictory_evidence: The linked ETH ComparatorChallenges file ends its exact_count_and_sat challenge declaration with `sorry` at line 938. The official formalization catalog separately maps the result to OAI/Algorithms/SubexponentialSAT/SqrtLogSpace/Final.lean, whose mapped theorem has a proof body. The challenge stub is therefore not evidence that no formal proof exists. No current repository commit was pinned, and no Lean build, dependency/axiom audit or exact paper-to-formal correspondence check was performed.

The linked local-smoothing ComparatorChallenges file has `sorry` bodies for six challenge entrypoints. OpenAI’s formalization catalog maps the related declarations to OAI/Analysis/Fourier/LocalSmoothing/Comparator.lean, where the inspected proof bodies invoke existing development theorems. The challenge file alone does not refute formal proof coverage. Build status, dependency closure and manuscript-to-formal scope remain unverified.

evidence_gaps.description: The PDFs were downloaded and their front matter/introductions were text-inspected, but the complete proof arguments, Lean source/dependency closure, configured build, and correspondence between paper theorems and formalized statements were not audited or run.
No independent complexity-theorist, analyst or mathematical-physics assessment of correctness, novelty or priority was found in this bounded release check.
The QCD and Standard Model artifacts are not public, so the announced physics theorem's assumptions and proof scope cannot yet be assessed from primary technical material.

The public ETH comparator challenge file has a `sorry`, while the formalization catalog separately maps exact_count_and_sat to SqrtLogSpace/Final.lean, which has a proof body. The exact commit, dependency/axiom closure and relationship between the formal statement and the manuscript have not been verified.

The public local-smoothing challenge file has six `sorry` bodies, while the formalization catalog separately maps the theorem declarations to LocalSmoothing/Comparator.lean, whose inspected proof bodies invoke existing development theorems. The exact revision, dependency/axiom closure and manuscript correspondence remain unverified.

brief.importance_rationale: If these foundational mathematical results are correct and novel, especially the reported ETH refutation, they could alter research directions across complexity theory, analysis and quantum field theory. Score 8 reflects consequence if true; the publisher's own announcement and Lean formalization do not establish correctness, novelty or acceptance.
limitations: OpenAI is the interested first-party source for the model outputs and mathematical results.

The two linked manuscript PDFs were downloaded and their abstract/introduction text was inspected, but this activation did not audit complete proofs, run a Lean build, inspect dependency closure or check paper-to-formal correspondence.
Lean formalization can support proof checking but does not by itself establish theorem interpretation, novelty, priority or external acceptance.
The physics claim is announced but its AI-produced artifacts are withheld; this record does not validate the theorem.
No independent specialist assessment, proof reproduction or community acceptance was established.

The ComparatorChallenges files contain admitted placeholders, but the repository instructions describe these as challenge configs and the catalog maps the relevant declarations to separate proof-source files; the challenge placeholders alone do not refute formal proof coverage.

The mapped ETH and local-smoothing proof files were read in the current unpinned main view. This activation did not run Lean, pin the exact revision, inspect full import/dependency closure or run axiom checks.
No independent specialist assessment, proof reproduction or community acceptance was established; exact correspondence between all manuscript claims and mapped formal statements remains unverified.

technical.claimed_result: OpenAI claims an all-dimensions local-smoothing result and an ETH refutation with Lean formalization, and announces a QCD/Standard Model existence proof whose artifacts are not yet public.

The catalog maps the ETH and local-smoothing declarations to separate source files with proof terms. This activation did not pin a revision, run Lean, audit imports/axioms or establish full manuscript-to-formal correspondence.

No independent proof audit, Lean build, acceptance or downstream research impact was established. technical.strongest_baseline: The local-smoothing manuscript discusses prior partial-dimensional results. OpenAI cites earlier results and names complexity theorists to shepherd the ETH work. This activation did not independently reconstruct either literature baseline or assess novelty.

brief.title: OpenAI releases AI-generated mathematical research claims with specialist-led review groups
brief.why_it_matters: If the mathematical claims withstand independent review, an AI-generated refutation of the Exponential Time Hypothesis and results in harmonic analysis and quantum field theory could materially change foundational research. This release also tests a new disclosure pattern that pairs public raw artifacts with independent expert-led explanation. Consequence is high, while correctness, novelty, priority and community acceptance remain unresolved.

other.title: OpenAI releases 722 AI-generated mathematics manuscripts across 372 result families with partial Lean formalization
other.summary: On October 6, OpenAI published a GitHub collection of mathematical manuscripts generated by an internal frontier model, alongside some Lean formalizations and process details. The repository README reports 722 manuscripts across 372 families and approximately 4,000 attempted problems. OpenAI says not all results are formalized and some unformalized work may contain errors. An independent mathematics advisory group calls the release an important first step, while saying mathematical assessment and human understanding remain to be done.
organizations: Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence
